title: Correlation header translator and SDK fastpath for low-overhead request observability
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Provide a tiny, deterministic translator that normalizes incoming correlation headers into Redwood's canonical request context plus an SDK fastpath API to attach that context to hotpath requests without allocation-heavy operations. Motivation: production services with short-lived requests (50-200ms) are sensitive to even small CPU and allocation overhead from tracing middleware. Existing instrumentation layers introduce object allocations and lock contention when reconstructing baggage/trace ids, which inflates p50/p95 in microservices and ingestion workers. Scope: build a header translator component that runs in the ingress path (edge proxy / internal gateway) and emits a compact 24-byte correlation token plus an optional fingerprint header. Provide SDK bindings (Go, Node, Python) that accept the compact token and attach it to requests using lock-free, preallocated context slots (fastpath). Must be compatible with current trace IDs and preserve sampling decisions. Non-goals: full OTEL conversion or replacing our full tracing stack. Constraints: maintain backward compatibility with existing clients that send X-Request-Id, Traceparent, Baggage, and our legacy X-RW-Context. Translator should be pluggable and deployable as a lightweight sidecar or ingress filter.
acceptance_criteria: Translator normalizes headers (Traceparent, Baggage, X-Request-Id, X-RW-Context) into a single X-RW-Ctx token with documented binary layout
SDK fastpath exposes a single call to attach the X-RW-Ctx token to outgoing requests with zero allocation in the common case
End-to-end latency regression <= 0.8ms p50 and <= 2ms p95 on our internal microservice benchmark for 100RPS bursts compared to baseline without instrumentation
Sampling decision and trace id propagation preserved for all supported header combinations
Automated tests cover translation permutations and gateway + SDK integration; integration test added to CI and nightly perf job
Migration docs and example code for Go/Node/Python in docs repo and a rollout plan with feature switch
